title: PicardExternalCoefficientsAffineLocalCohomology
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], X,Y schemes [def-pc-scheme], and f:X -> Spec(k), g:Y -> Spec(k) morphisms. Assume X is quasi-compact and the diagonal of f is affine. Let F,G be quasi-coherent modules on X,Y [pqf-def-coherent]. Put E=pr1^*F tensor pr2^*G [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. For every affine open V of Y and every q >= 0, there is an isomorphism of additive groups H^q(pr2^{-1}(V),E) [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] with H^q(X,F) tensor_k Gamma(V,G restricted to V). The first factor uses the scalarCohomology k-action induced by f; the second uses scalarObj for V -> Y -> Spec(k). There are no acyclicity hypotheses and no quasi-compactness or affine-diagonal hypothesis on Y.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, affine-open calculation and degree-zero direct-image formula; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BED

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover U_i of X. The affine diagonal criterion makes all finite intersections affine. The inverse image of the affine open V under pr2 is the product X times V. Open-immersion pullback agrees with restriction; its compatibility with composition identifies the restriction of E with the external tensor of F and G restricted to V. The products U_i times V and their intersections are affine.

On every product chart, affine pullback and tensor-section comparisons identify sections with F(U_intersection) tensor_k G(V). Their pure-tensor formulas commute with restrictions, so the Cech differential is d tensor 1. Finite products over tuples of cover indices commute with tensor: send the tensor of a tuple with t to the tuple of tensors; invert it using the finitely many coordinate inclusions.

Tensoring with the vector space G(V) is exact. It preserves the cycles and boundaries and hence cohomology of the Cech complex. The affine Cech comparison identifies the first-factor cohomology with H^q(X,F), with k-action restricted along f. The same comparison on X times V identifies its Cech cohomology with the cohomology of E on the inverse-image open; restricting injective resolutions computes precisely openModuleCohomology. Forget the scalar action to obtain the stated isomorphism of additive groups. This applies in degree zero and to empty schemes, empty V and zero modules.

theorem picardExternalCupCoefficients_affine_local_cohomology
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    [CompactSpace X] [IsAffineHom (pullback.diagonal f)]
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (q : ℕ) :
    Nonempty
      (((RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace q
        ((pullback.snd f g) ⁻¹ᵁ V)).obj (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)) ≅
        AddCommGrpCat.of (scalarCohomology f F q ⊗[k]
          scalarObj (V.ι ≫ g) (G.restrict V.ι) (Opposite.op ⊤)))
